source: proposed by gpt-6.1-sol (Codex, reasoning high) 2026-10-07 from candidates by name similarity and shared Strong number; every fold read by Claude (lead), all 23 accepted; 4 unsure (bether-2, hermons, magdolum, thelme) and 76 distinct left unfolded

folds.reason: Gomorrha is the Greek NT spelling of Gomorrah, as in MAT 10:15. Both records explicitly share G1116.
G2455 includes Judah as the tribe named in HEB 7:14 and HEB 8:8, both attached to judah-6. The Judea candidates represent the geographic region under different headwords.
Sychem is the Greek NT spelling of Shechem in ACT 7:16. The Tell Balatah candidate explicitly shares G4966.
Chaldaean G5466 is the gentilic used in 'land of the Chaldaeans' in ACT 7:4. The Chaldea candidate explicitly includes this Greek headword and Strong number.
Charran is the Greek NT spelling of Haran in ACT 7:2,4. Both records share G5488 and refer to Harran.
Ish-tob (H382) in 2SA 10:6,8 is commonly understood as 'men of Tob,' referring to the land of Tob known from JDG 11:3,5.
Alternate spelling of the Oak of Weeping where Deborah was buried, GEN 35:8. Both records share H439.
Dan-jaan in 2SA 24:6 is conventionally identified with northern Dan. The Tel Dan candidate explicitly includes the alias Dan Jaan, although the geographical identification is debated.
H1996 denotes Hamon-gog, the burial valley named in EZK 39:11 and 39:15. Those are exactly the candidate valley's references.
Bashan-Havoth-jair is the fuller regional name for Jair's settlements in DEU 3:14. The candidate includes that verse and the corresponding Havoth-jair aliases.
Hazar-hatticon and Hazer-hatticon are spelling variants of the border locality in EZK 47:16. The candidate includes the exact Hazar Hatticon alias.
Charashim (H2798) names the craftsmen’s valley in 1 Chronicles 4:14; Ge-harashim explicitly includes the alias 'valley of Charashim' and that verse.
Carmelite (H3761) is the gentilic of the town Carmel, used for Nabal in 1 Samuel 30:5. The settlement candidate also carries 'Carmelitess'; Mount Carmel is a separate geographical referent.
Ittah-kazin is an alternative spelling of Eth-kazin, the Zebulun boundary settlement in JOS 19:13. The candidate explicitly includes the label Ittah-kazin.
Padan is the shortened form of Paddan-aram used in GEN 48:7. Both records identify H6307, and the candidate includes Paddan as an alias.
Kirjath-arba is the former name of Hebron, explicitly identified in GEN 23:2 and JOS 14:15. The Hebron candidate includes Kiriath-arba and shares H7153.
Shebah and Shiba are alternative renderings of the well named by Isaac in GEN 26:33. Both records identify H7656.
H8613 is the Tophet form used in ISA 30:33, a variant associated with Topheth in the Valley of Hinnom. The candidate already includes ISA 30:33 among its occurrences.
The Nahor candidate explicitly identifies its location as Nahuru, matching the settlement near Haran associated with GEN 24:10.
The Pethor candidate explicitly gives Pitru as another name, matching the Mesopotamian settlement associated with Balaam in NUM 22:5 and DEU 23:4.

Beth-togarmah explicitly identifies its modern referent as another name for Tegarama and is likewise classified as a settlement. Togarmah has the same Ezekiel passages but lacks this explicit settlement identification.
The distinguisher identifies Joseph called Barsabbas, surnamed Justus, the candidate to replace Judas Iscariot in ACT 1:23.
The distinguisher identifies Judas called Barsabbas, sent with Silas to Antioch in ACT 15:22–32. Joseph also bears G923 but is a different person.
